title: Recall Studio Question Batch
description: Portable AI-generated deck/question import contract. Syntactic validation plus application semantic invariants. Version 1.0.0. All free-text fields accept Markdown (GFM) and LaTeX math delimited by $...$ (inline) or $$...$$ (display), rendered with KaTeX (incl. mhchem \\ce{}); fenced code blocks are syntax-highlighted; ```mermaid and ```svg fences render as diagrams (sanitized); GFM tables and image URLs are supported; raw HTML is rendered after allowlist sanitizing (no scripts, iframes, event handlers or javascript: URLs).

language.description: BCP-47 language tag, e.g. ko or en

relativeTolerance.description: relative tolerance as a fraction of |value|

unit.description: display unit, shown next to the input; the learner enters only the number

answer.description: optional: when acceptedAnswers are given the typed answer is auto-graded; otherwise the learner self-checks against the back side

cloze_bank.description: Cloze whose blanks are filled from one shared word bank (each bank item usable once; extra items are distractors). prompt uses {{id}} placeholders like cloze.

bank.description: shared word bank; may contain distractors; each item fills at most one blank

code_cloze.description: Fill-in-the-blank inside a code block; graded per blank, case-sensitive by default (normalization.caseFold defaults to false here).

matrix.description: Row × column check grid (attribute tables, truth tables, adjacency); answer.cells lists the cells that must be checked. Graded per row.

selection.description: multiple = any number of cells per row (checkboxes); single = exactly one column per row (radios)

numeric_grid.description: Table of numeric answers (matrices, computed tables, timelines as rows × year); each answer cell has its own tolerance.

relativeTolerance.description: relative tolerance as a fraction of |value|

list_answer.description: Order-independent set of short answers ("name three …"); each entry is matched against an unused item; correct when at least `required` distinct items are named and no entry is wrong.

required.description: how many distinct items the learner must name (default: all)

image_hotspot.description: Click the correct area(s) on an image or inline SVG; the learner places one marker per target region. Regions are never sent to the client before grading.

svg.description: inline <svg …>…</svg> markup (sanitized; no scripts or external references)

regions.description: coordinates normalized to 0..1 of the image width/height (circle r relative to width and height independently)

parsons.description: Parsons problem: arrange shuffled code lines (plus optional distractors) in order and set each line's indentation level.

find_and_fix.description: Find the wrong segment(s) in a passage/code and type the corrected value; graded per expected fix (located + fixed), extra selections are wrong.

coordinate_point.description: Place point(s) on a coordinate plane; each expected point is matched to the closest unused placed point within its tolerance.

tolerance.description: euclidean distance allowed (default 0 = exact after snapping)

regex_answer.description: Write a regular expression that matches every positive example and no negative example (JavaScript syntax; pattern ≤ 200 chars, nested quantifiers rejected).

fullMatch.description: true = the whole string must match (pattern is wrapped in ^(?:…)$)

modelPattern.description: a reference solution shown after grading; must satisfy every example

$comment: Semantic validation outside JSON Schema: Within a deck, question IDs are unique. | IDs within each choices/items/left/right/blanks array must be unique. | single_choice.answer.choiceId must occur in choices. | multiple_choice.answer.choiceIds must all occur in choices, include >=2 and be a proper subset of choices. | cloze prompt placeholders {{id}} and blank IDs must be exactly equal. | ordering.answer.orderedIds must be a permutation of items[].id. | matching.answer.pairs must create a bijection of left and right IDs. | essay.answer.rubric[].maxPoints must sum to answer.maxScore. | Every answer must be verifiably supported by explanatory rationale. | Text fields may contain Markdown and LaTeX ($...$, $$...$$). acceptedAnswers are plain strings compared after normalization, never LaTeX. | Extended types (additive, v1.0.0-compatible): numeric (|given-value| <= max(tolerance, |value|*relativeTolerance)), cloze_select (prompt {{id}} placeholders == blanks ids; answerOptionId in options), statement_set (statement ids unique), categorize (item.categoryId in categories; ids unique), two_tier (answer.choiceId in choices and answer.reasonId in reasons), recall_card (self-checked unless acceptedAnswers given), stepwise (step ids unique; graded per step), highlight (answer.segmentIds subset of segments ids). | cloze_bank (placeholders = blank ids; bankItemId in bank; each bank item used at most once) | code_cloze (placeholders in code = blank ids) | matrix (cells reference rows/columns, no duplicates; selection=single → exactly one cell per row) | numeric_grid (cells/given reference rows/columns, each row×column used once) | list_answer (required ≤ items.length) | image_hotspot (exactly one of image.url/svg; answer.regionIds ⊂ regions; polygon ≥ 3 points) | parsons (answer.lines ids = permutation of lines ids; distractor ids disjoint) | find_and_fix (fix segmentIds ⊂ segments, unique, at least one untouched segment) | coordinate_point (points inside the plane; ids unique) | regex_answer (shouldMatch ∩ shouldNotMatch = ∅; modelPattern compiles, is safe and satisfies every example).
